intro.title: What you want to build
paragraphs: Now let’s look at your specific venture.
What do you want to achieve? What can you realistically contribute? And which expectations, rules, or boundaries matter to you?
Some things may already be clear, while others are not. Both are fine. Open questions can help identify important conversations later.

screens.title: How would you like to work together?
screens.transition: When responsibilities are clearly defined, how much freedom would you like within your area?

screens.title: How much visibility would you like into each other’s work?
screens.transition: Good collaboration means different things to different people. Some want to be involved early; others prefer to wait until things are more concrete.

screens.title: What do you want this venture to become?
screens.transition: People build businesses for many reasons. What matters most to you in this venture?

screens.title: When things do not go to plan
screens.transition: Not every venture develops as expected. What would matter to you then?

screens.title: How do you want to make decisions?
screens.transition: Differences are part of working together. The question is how you reach a decision despite them.

screens.title: Money, risk, and safeguards
screens.transition: People have very different limits around money and personal risk. This is about what realistically works for you, rather than what seems brave or right.

screens.title: When two things matter at once
screens.transition: Sometimes two things both make sense, but pull in different directions.

screens.title: Your personal boundaries
screens.transition: Finally, your personal boundaries. Not everything has to be negotiable.

closing.title: All done.
closing.text: Take another look at your responses. When everything reflects your situation, you can finish this part.
closing.subline: Submitting completes this round. Your responses will become visible to the members of this team after you submit.
